summary: A Jetson TX2 forum thread in which user Houber asked why calling OpenCV's imshow() inside a VPI (Vision Programming Interface 1.1) C++ program failed, while imread() and imwrite() worked. NVIDIA's AastaLLL replied that cv::imshow works in their environment, recommended ssh -X for window forwarding, and provided a diff to the VPI 01-convolve_2d sample that links opencv_highgui and adds cv::imshow and cv::waitKey calls. Houber reported the problem was solved, and the topic was closed automatically in March 2023.
one_line: NVIDIA forum thread on a Jetson TX2 failing to show OpenCV imshow() output inside a VPI 1.1 C++ program, resolved with ssh -X and highgui linking.
key_facts: The thread was posted on February 20, 2023 in the NVIDIA Developer Forums Jetson TX2 category.
The user Houber was using VPI version 1.1 on a Jetson TX2 platform with C++.
imread() and imwrite() worked in the user's VPI program, but adding imshow() from OpenCV caused an error.
The user's base code was the VPI sample program 01-convolve_2d (2D Image Convolution).
The user added the include <opencv2/highgui.hpp> and called imshow("img", cvOut) after imwrite("edges_" + strBackend + ".png", cvOut).
AastaLLL from NVIDIA stated that cv::imshow works well in their environment.
AastaLLL advised connecting with ssh -X (for example, ssh -X nvidia@[IP]) to allow window forwarding when linked over SSH.
The suggested CMakeLists.txt change modifies the non-legacy OpenCV branch to link opencv_imgcodecs and opencv_highgui.
The suggested main.cpp change adds an include of opencv2/highgui/highgui.hpp and calls cv::imshow("output", cvOut) followed by cv::waitKey(0).
Houber replied on February 20, 2023 at 6:13am that the problem was solved.
The topic was automatically closed on March 6, 2023, 14 days after the last reply.
